attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway for the private "lan" network (10.50.50.0/24, egress:false) so node2 and node3 (Ubuntu 16.04) reach the internet through it, implemented via an Ansible playbook run from the control_node (node4). node1's eth1 got 10.50.50.1/24 plus a source-NAT masquerade rule out eth0 (its internet-facing mgmt interface); node2/node3's ens7 got static lan IPs (10.50.50.2/.3) and a lower-metric default route via node1, so default egress genuinely transits node1's NAT (confirmed via NAT rule packet counters and conntrack entries showing translated flows, plus curl 200 to example.com). Ubuntu 16.04's python2.7/3.5 are incompatible with ansible-core 2.20's module_utils, so that play uses the python-free ansible.builtin.raw module; VyOS is configured via a templated bash script sourcing the VyOS script-template envelope, executed with ansible.builtin.command. Bootstrapped SSH key-based access from node4 to all three managed nodes first (added node4's pubkey to node1's vyos user via VyOS config, and to antrieb users on node2/node3), since none pre-existed. Completed the mandatory sequential single-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, verifying changed boot IDs and full recovery for each, then re-ran the playbook post-restart to confirm idempotency and persistence.
